sentences.text: The accident in question is not in dispute.

The KSRTC however contends that the disability taken by the Tribunal at 10% on the premise that the claimant has suffered a fracture to the vertebra at L1 and L2 was not correct, since the wound certificate did not disclose such a fracture.

3. The claimant, on the other hand, contends that the discharge summary as well as the entire case sheet categorically states that the claimant had suffered a fracture of L1 and L2 vertebra and therefore, assessment of whole body disability of the claimant at 10% cannot be found fault with.
4.
It was also argued that the notional income of the claimant determined by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- is improper, since the accident is of the year 2014.
5. As far as the ground raised by the KSRTC is concerned, no doubt, in the wound certificate, it has not been mentioned that the claimant had suffered fracture of L1 and L2 vertebra.
6. It is also true that the doctor who was examined has stated that he cannot comment on the said fractures since it has not been mentioned in the wound certificate.

However, the discharge summary which was produced as Ex.P-7 states that the claimant was diagnosed with the following problems:
"RTA-Mild Head injury - Forehead laceration Multiple blunt trauma to Back, right knee, Fore arm CLW over Right forearm (Extensor Tendon injury) Fracture of L1 &
L2 - (L) Transverse Process ?(L) 8th Rib Fracture."
7.
This diagnosis clearly indicates that the claimant did have a fracture of L1 and L2 vertebra and also sustained 8th rib fracture.
8. In the light of this discharge summary, the assessment of disability at 10% to the whole body of the claimant cannot be found fault with.
9. The appeal of the KSRTC is therefore dismissed.

sentences.text: In arriving at the said compensation, the Tribunal has determined the monthly notional income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/-.
Since the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined a sum of Rs.8,500/- as notional income for the accidents of the year 2014, it would be appropriate to apply the said income.
12. The claimant was aged about 34 years and hence, appropriate multiplier applicable is '16'.
13. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a compensation of Rs.1,63,200/- (Rs.8,500/- x 12 x '16' x 10%) towards loss of future earnings due to disability.
14. In my view, the award in respect of all other heads is just and proper and do not require any enhancement.
